items.followUp: Name and explain any four layers of the OSI network model.

rubric.why: Shows that the Physical layer carries bits or signals over the communication medium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and stating a correct transmission function.

rubric.why: Shows that the Data Link layer organizes bits into frames or manages communication on a direct link.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and stating a correct function.

rubric.why: Shows that the Network layer handles routing or logical addressing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and stating a correct function.

rubric.why: Shows that the Transport layer provides end-to-end delivery or reliable transmission.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the layer and stating a correct function.

modelAnswer: The Physical layer transmits raw bits as electrical, optical or radio signals over a communication medium.
The Data Link layer organizes bits into frames and handles communication between directly connected devices.
The Network layer provides logical addressing and selects routes for data packets between networks.
The Transport layer provides end-to-end delivery of data and may ensure reliable transmission.

items.followUp: Explain how software piracy differs from copyright.

rubric.why: Defines software piracy as unauthorized or illegal copying, use or distribution of software.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for explaining that software is copied, used or distributed illegally or without permission; award 1 mark for identifying it only as illegal copying.

rubric.why: Explains that copyright is legal protection giving a creator control over use or copying of original work.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for explaining both the legal protection and the creator's rights; award 1 mark for identifying copyright only as legal protection.

modelAnswer: Software piracy is the illegal copying, installation, use or distribution of software without the owner's permission or a valid licence.
Copyright is the legal protection given to the creator of an original work, giving the creator control over its copying, use and distribution.

items.followUp: List five questions you would ask to understand a problem before solving it.

rubric.why: Recognizes that understanding a problem involves identifying the problem, available inputs and required output.
rubric.description: Identify the problem, inputs and output
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the problem and the supplied information and required result.

rubric.why: Recognizes that the required processing and any conditions, constraints or special cases must be considered.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the operations needed and relevant conditions or limitations.

modelAnswer: What is the problem, and what inputs or information are given?
What output or result is required?
What processing or operations are needed to obtain the result?
What conditions or constraints must be followed?
Is there any special case or limitation that must be considered?

items.followUp: Define HTML and state its main purpose.

rubric.why: Defines a mark-up language as using tags or marks to describe content.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a mark-up language uses tags or marks.

rubric.why: Explains that the tags describe or organize the structure or content of a document.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that tags describe or structure the content.

modelAnswer: A mark-up language uses tags or marks to describe and organize the structure of text and other content.
